transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, Doc. Well, I guess what brings me in is... this memorial I'm planning for my brother. It’s just gotten a lot bigger than I meant it to. 

I’ve been spending most of my days working on it lately—chasing down specific songs, calling folks up, planning out these big displays and even trips. My wife is the one who really pushed me to come see you. She says I’ve completely pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else I normally do. So, I suppose that's why I'm here.
{"intent":"Assess for a decreased need for sleep suggesting a manic or hypomanic episode.","question":"During this period of intensive memorial planning, have you needed less sleep than usual?"]
I haven't really noticed needing less sleep. I mean, I'm busy with the planning, but I still go to bed around the same time I usually do. I haven't been staying up all night or anything like that.
Do you feel driven to carry out the memorial planning by unwanted thoughts or urges that are difficult to resist?

No, it's not like that. It's just... something I really want to do for him. It doesn't feel like an unwanted urge or anything forcing me. I just want to make sure it's perfect, you know? It's important to me.
How long ago did your brother die?
He passed away about two months ago. That's when I started working on his tribute, and I've been at it pretty much ever since.
Do you find yourself longing intensely for your brother or preoccupied with thoughts of him most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I miss him, sure... but I'm not just sitting around crying or longing for him all day. I'm mostly just focused on getting this memorial done right. I think about him when I'm working on it, but it's not like I'm overwhelmed by it every second of the day.
Since your brother died, have you had persistent difficulty accepting that he is gone?
No, I know he's gone. I've accepted that. I just want to make sure his memorial is exactly what he deserves. I'm not in denial about him being dead or anything like that.
Since your brother died, have you been feeling persistently sad or hopeless?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I have moments where I'm sad, sure, but not all the time. And I definitely don't feel hopeless. Like I said, I've got all this work to do for his memorial, so I'm mostly just keeping busy with that. I don't really feel down or anything.
Since your brother died, have you been feeling persistently anxious or excessively worried?

No, not really. I'm not sitting around worrying or feeling anxious about things. I'm just... focused, you know? Like I've got this big project with the memorial, and that's where my energy is going. I don't feel nervous or anything like that.
Since your brother died, have you often felt nervous or on edge?

No, I don't feel nervous or on edge. I think that's pretty much the same as what you just asked, isn't it? I'm not feeling anxious or jittery. I'm just putting all my energy into getting the memorial right.
